_meta.purpose: Human-adjudicated bad keys for BFCL v4 multi-turn. Drop these ids from N before computing appropriate-action accuracy, the A2 penalty, or any rank statistic.
_meta.source: copied verbatim from the sealed exclusion list (phase4_exclude.json, 31 ids, approved 2026-06-09 + 4 amendments 2026-06-11); reasons transcribed from the authors' review notes and the amendment note in that list
_meta.method: mechanical prefilter (151 candidates), then manual review by the authors against the simulator source.
_meta.kept_rationale: base_196: GOLD omits priority and takes the function default, which is the reasonable reading of a user request that never mentions priority. miss_param_29: GOLD paraphrases the user's previous message where models wrote it verbatim - an alternative-path (A2) case, not an objective key error.
_meta.caveat: long_context 28 / 32 and base 176 carry an unresolved padding caveat and were excluded under the authors' uncertain-drop policy, not as proven key errors. Sensitivity to the whole list is reported (no-exclude, N=200).

families.A: objective GOLD error or GOLD contradicting/fabricating relative to the user request
families.B: disputed GOLD constant or invented argument, excluded under the uncertain-drop policy
families.D: task defect / no-op perturbation found during the inter-annotator agreement pilot

_meta.note: Categories are variants of shared base scenarios, so one scenario ruling applies to every category in which that scenario appears (e.g. scenario 4 is bad in all four).

bad_keys.reason: Task asks to sort the report file's lines before tweeting; GOLD tweet text is a word-level reshuffle that no real sort can produce (report.txt reads as a single line in the simulator, so sort is a no-op). Single-line assumption not byte-verified, excluded under the uncertain-drop policy.

bad_keys.family: A. GOLD alters content the user asked to send verbatim
bad_keys.reason: User asks to tweet the file content 'exactly as it is'; the file contains JSON quotes but GOLD's post_tweet content has every quote stripped, contradicting 'exactly'.

bad_keys.family: B. GOLD text contradicts the user
bad_keys.reason: User states the trip is on December 15, 2026; GOLD's ticket description says December 15, 2023, so a faithful model writing 2026 mismatches on the description string.

bad_keys.family: B. GOLD invents an unrequested argument
bad_keys.reason: User asks to draft a complaint titled 'Unsatisfactory Customer Support' and never mentions priority; GOLD hardcodes priority=4 and an empty description. Adjudicated together with scenario 187 as the 'invented priority' family.

bad_keys.family: A. GOLD contradicts an explicit user requirement
bad_keys.reason: User asks for a 'high-priority' ticket and the simulator's priority scale is 1-5 with 5 highest; GOLD writes priority=4, so a model that correctly writes 5 is failed.
